title: MCP Apps
summary: Integrate the official MCP Apps extension and SDK to deliver interactive UIs from MCP servers into compliant AI chat hosts.

sections.heading: Official MCP Apps standard
body: MCP Apps is the official Model Context Protocol extension for interactive user interfaces delivered by MCP servers. The stable specification is version 2026-01-26 (SEP-1865).

The canonical implementation repository is https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps. It contains the protocol specification, TypeScript SDK, generated schemas, examples, testing host, and Agent Skills.
The official documentation portal is https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/. Use the specification as the protocol authority and the SDK/API documentation for implementation details.

sections.heading: Server → Host → View
body: MCP Apps uses three roles: the MCP server registers tools and UI resources; the host is the conversational client that embeds and mediates the UI; and the View is the interactive application running in a sandboxed iframe.
A tool links to a UI resource through the ui:// URI scheme and UI metadata. The host retrieves the resource, renders it securely, and proxies communication between the View and the MCP server.

The View communicates with its host using MCP JSON-RPC over postMessage. This preserves MCP semantics while allowing interactive actions, tool calls, resource reads, model-context updates, and host UI requests.

examples.code:
MCP Server
  ├─ Tool
  │   └─ _meta.ui.resourceUri → ui://...
  └─ UI Resource (HTML)
           │
           ▼
      Host / Chat Client
           │
     sandboxed iframe
           ▼
          View
       App + UI logic

sections.heading: SDK roles and packages
body: The @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps package supports the three implementation boundaries: View authors build interactive Apps, host authors embed Views with AppBridge, and server authors register tools/resources with UI metadata.

The current ext-apps package exposes the main App API, React helpers, AppBridge, message transport, server helpers, and generated protocol types. The repository also publishes the schema used by the SDK.
The current official package metadata identifies @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps version 2.0.0 and Node.js >=20 as the runtime baseline.
bullets: Protocol types/schema: @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps and its generated schema

sections.heading: Quickstart
body: For a new TypeScript MCP App, start with the official Quickstart. The standard pattern is Tool + UI Resource: register a tool, register the HTML resource, link the resource from tool metadata, then let a compliant host render the View.

For a server-side implementation, the official examples use the MCP TypeScript server packages together with ext-apps and Zod. Build the UI as a self-contained HTML bundle that the MCP server can expose as a resource.
Before shipping, test against the repository's basic-host reference implementation and at least one real MCP Apps-compatible host.

sections.heading: Security and capability negotiation
body: MCP Apps is an optional extension. Hosts advertise support for the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui extension during MCP initialization, including the supported UI MIME type. Servers should check that capability before registering UI-enabled behavior and should provide meaningful text fallback behavior.
Views run in sandboxed iframes and do not receive direct access to the host DOM, cookies, or storage. Communication is mediated through postMessage and the MCP Apps protocol.
External network access is constrained by declarative CSP metadata. Keep allowed origins narrow, scope app-only tools deliberately, and treat UI resources and tool metadata as auditable inputs.

sections.heading: Agent Skills for MCP Apps
body: The official ext-apps repository ships four Agent Skills that can be used by compatible AI coding agents to accelerate MCP App development and migration.
These skills are directly relevant to the Velclaw agent workflow because they map to scaffold, migration, server integration, and hybrid web-app conversion tasks.
bullets: create-mcp-app — scaffold a new MCP App
migrate-oai-app — migrate an existing OpenAI App to MCP Apps
add-app-to-server — add interactive UI to existing MCP server tools
convert-web-app — add MCP App support to an existing web application
